$comment: The locales THIS repo translates into, and the subset whose errors gate CI.
`targets` is every locale this repo translates into. A locale belongs here
once its content does. Listing one whose files have not landed yet would make
every script iterate a locale with nothing in it, so the list grows in the
same change that brings the content.
`productionTargets` is the subset held to a production standard, and it is the
only thing `scripts/validate.mjs` exits non-zero on. Errors outside it are
still found, printed and counted, exactly as before; they just do not gate.
The reason is that `targets` spans locales at wildly different stages, from
served-to-real-users down to a first bootstrap sample, and a gate that is
permanently red across all of them tells you nothing: it stops being read
within a month, and then a real regression in a live locale goes unnoticed
underneath the noise. Scoping the gate is what makes red mean "fix this now".
Provenance of the current 9: the 7 marked "live": true in the review site's
src/data/status.json (fr, uk, it, el, es-419, es-ES, hu), plus pt-BR and pt-PT,
which iHiD holds to the same standard ahead of them going live.
This is deliberately NOT the same list as the front-end's
app/lib/production-locales.json (which lib/locales.ts turns into its
SUPPORTED_LOCALES), the subset actually SERVED. The two
answer different questions and are expected to differ:
- a locale is held to the standard HERE before it is served THERE, which is
exactly the pt-BR/pt-PT case: they must go green here first, so promoting
them there is a decision and not a discovery;
- the front-end list carries "en", and this one never can. English is not
stored in this repo at all (see ENGLISH-SOURCE.md), so it is not a target
locale here and `assertTargetLocale` refuses it by name.
Do not "fix" the divergence by syncing the two files. Moving a locale from
one to the other is the go-live step, and it is one-way: it joins this list,
goes green, and only then joins the front-end's.
`source` is not a target locale. It is the read-only English mirror, and
every script refuses to write to it. See CLAUDE.md.
